mainTopic: The end of the debate on destroying חמץ (רבי יהודה's refuted proof and whether crumbling is needed), and the new משנה about חמץ kept over פסח
overview: This עמוד finishes the debate about how to destroy חמץ and then begins a new משנה. רבי יהודה tries a second proof that חמץ must be burned: חמץ and נותר both fall under 'בל תותירו', so חמץ should be burned like נותר. The חכמים refute him from his own view, since he holds that אשם תלוי and חטאת העוף הבא על הספק, which are also under 'בל תותירו', are buried. רבי יהודה is silent, and רב יוסף, אביי and רבא each give a folk saying about being defeated by your own handiwork. The גמרא then asks whether the חכמים require crumbling חמץ before throwing it into the sea, and notes the same question about grinding an idol. רבה and רב יוסף reason in opposite directions, each is backed by one ברייתא and challenged by the other, and the גמרא answers both challenges by splitting the cases. Next comes a new משנה: a גוי's חמץ that was kept over פסח is permitted for benefit, but a Jew's is forbidden. The גמרא asks who wrote this משנה and begins quoting a ברייתא with the views of רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון and רבי יוסי הגלילי, a discussion that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבי יהודה offers a new proof from leftover sacrificial meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה argues that because both נותר and חמץ fall under 'בל תותירו', חמץ must be burned just as נותר is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה came back and made a different argument: נותר (leftover sacrificial meat) is included in 'Do not leave over,' and חמץ is also included in 'Do not leave over.' Just as נותר is burned, so too חמץ is burned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה's first proof was rejected, so he tries a new argument that compares חמץ to נותר to show that חמץ must be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared feature this time is 'בל תותירו': both items become forbidden once their time runs out. Since the תורה says נותר is destroyed by burning, רבי יהודה says חמץ, which shares this 'leftover' quality, must also be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: He came back and argued it with a different line of reasoning
Sacrificial meat left over past the time it may be eaten
Just as ... so too ... (the formula of a comparison)

steps.confusionAlert: חמץ is not literally a sacrifice. רבי יהודה is comparing them because both become forbidden after a set time. That is the sense in which חמץ is 'left over'.

phrases.aramaic: חָזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְדָנוֹ דִּין אַחֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda came back and argued a different line of reasoning:
phrases.notes: His earlier comparison was refuted, so he offers a new one.

phrases.english: Leftover sacrificial meat is included in 'Do not leave over,'
and leavened bread is included in 'Do not leave over.'
phrases.notes: After its time, owning חמץ violates בל יראה and בל ימצא, so it too may not be 'left over'.

phrases.english: Just as leftover meat is destroyed by burning,
so too leavened bread is destroyed by burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְדָנוֹ דִּין אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי יהודה's earlier proof, which the חכמים had rejected on the previous עמוד.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's ruling that חמץ must be destroyed specifically by burning
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to נותר, based on the shared feature of 'בל תותירו'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמץ should be burned like נותר because both fall under 'בל תותירו'.

steps.title: The Sages refute him using doubtful offerings
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים point out that אשם תלוי and חטאת העוף הבא על הספק are also under 'בל תותירו', yet רבי יהודה himself rules they are buried, not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: By your own words, אשם תלוי and a bird חטאת brought for a doubt prove otherwise. They are included in 'Do not leave over.' We say they are burned, but you say they are buried!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים knock down רבי יהודה's new comparison by showing a case where his own opinion contradicts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'בל תותירו' automatically meant 'must be burned,' then every offering under 'בל תותירו' would have to be burned. But רבי יהודה himself says these doubtful offerings are buried. So by his own logic, 'בל תותירו' does not require burning, and the comparison to נותר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'suspended' guilt-offering, brought when one is unsure whether he sinned
A bird sin-offering brought in a case of doubt
According to your own words or opinion
Will prove (a counterexample that disproves the comparison)

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying these offerings are buried. They hold the offerings are burned. Their point is that רבי יהודה holds they are buried, so he cannot claim that 'בל תותירו' always means burning.

phrases.english: They said to him:
An uncertain guilt-offering and a bird sin-offering
that is brought in a case of doubt
will prove the point against you, according to your own words,
for they are included in 'Do not leave over.'
For we say they are destroyed by burning,
but you say they are destroyed by burial!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אָשָׁם תָּלוּי וְחַטַּאת הָעוֹף הַבָּא עַל הַסָּפֵק לִדְבָרֶיךָ יוֹכִיחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the comparison made in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole comparison between חמץ and נותר based on 'בל תותירו'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'בל תותירו' does not by itself require burning. רבי יהודה himself rules that אשם תלוי and חטאת העוף הבא על הספק, which are also under 'בל תותירו', are buried.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic 'לדבריך' refutation. The challenger defeats the proof using the other person's own position, so he has no room to argue back.

steps.title: רבי יהודה has no reply
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה is silent, which shows that the refutation stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The exchange ends: רבי יהודה has no answer, so his second proof is left refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silence here means he accepted that this particular proof fails. It does not mean he gave up his ruling that חמץ is burned. Only this derivation is defeated.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent (he had no response)

steps.whatToRemember: Both of רבי יהודה's comparisons (to נותר) were refuted. His second proof failed because of his own ruling about doubtful offerings.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה's silence does not mean he retracted his position in the משנה. It only means this specific proof could not be defended.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda was silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the debate of steps 1 and 2 by showing the refutation was not answered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה's 'בל תותירו' comparison is refuted and goes unanswered.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the carpenter is burned by his own spoon
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a folk saying: the strongest attack on רבי יהודה came from his own opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is what people say: In the spoon the carpenter carved, the mustard will burn him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף comments on the debate with a popular saying. He is not adding a new legal point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A carpenter carves a spoon and then gets burned by hot mustard served in it. In the same way, רבי יהודה was defeated by a tool he made himself: his own ruling that the doubtful offerings are buried.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a folk proverb)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
This is what people say:
The spoon that the carpenter carved,
in it the mustard will burn him.
phrases.notes: One is hurt by his own handiwork.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the refutation in step 2 and רבי יהודה's silence in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה was refuted by his own ruling, like a carpenter burned by his own spoon.

steps.title: אביי: the maker of the stocks sits in them
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a second proverb with the same message: a person is paid back through his own handiwork.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The one who made the stocks sits in the stocks. He is paid back by his own handiwork.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds another popular saying that makes the same point as רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stocks are a wooden device for locking a prisoner's feet. The craftsman who built them ends up trapped in them, just as רבי יהודה was trapped by his own ruling. The second proverb strengthens the message and adds no new law.

keyTerms.meaning: Stocks (a wooden device for confining a prisoner)
From the work of his own hands

steps.whatToRemember: Main lesson of this section: רבי יהודה's 'בל תותירו' proof fails because of his own ruling about doubtful offerings. רב יוסף and אביי each sum this up with a proverb about being defeated by your own creation.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The maker of the stocks sits in the stocks;
he is repaid through his own handiwork.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel proverb alongside רב יוסף's in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is repaid through his own handiwork, as רבי יהודה was refuted by his own opinion.

steps.title: רבא's proverb: shot by his own arrows
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a third saying with the same idea: רבי יהודה was defeated by his own ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The arrow-maker is killed by his own arrows. He is paid back by the work of his own hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives one more folk saying to describe how the חכמים refuted רבי יהודה using his own ruling. This closes the discussion about רבי יהודה's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב יוסף and אביי before him, רבא adds no new law. His image fits the case well: רבי יהודה's own ruling, that אשם תלוי is buried, became the 'arrow' that defeated his argument for burning חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: The work of his own hands

steps.whatToRemember: Three אמוראים (רב יוסף, אביי, רבא) all describe the same idea: רבי יהודה's proof was refuted by his own ruling.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The arrow-maker is killed by his own arrows —
he is paid back through his own handiwork.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third parallel proverb after רב יוסף and אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person can be defeated by his own position, as רבי יהודה was.

steps.title: Does throwing חמץ into the sea require crumbling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה and asks whether crumbling is needed for both the wind and the sea, or only for the wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: he crumbles it and scatters it, etc. A question was asked: What do they mean? He crumbles it and scatters it to the wind, and he also crumbles it and throws it into the sea? Or perhaps he crumbles it and scatters it to the wind, but he may throw it into the sea whole, just as it is?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the חכמים's method of destroying חמץ and asks exactly what they meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions crumbling and two ways of getting rid of the חמץ (wind or sea). The question is whether 'crumble' applies to both methods. One option: crumbling is always needed. The other option: crumbling is needed only for the wind, because a whole loaf will not blow away, but the sea can take the loaf whole.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised to them (an open question)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: he crumbles and scatters, etc.
A question was raised: what are they saying?
He crumbles and scatters it to the wind,
and he crumbles and throws it into the sea?
Or perhaps: he crumbles and scatters it to the wind,
but he may throw it into the sea whole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי יהודה and turns to explain the חכמים's view in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is crumbling required before throwing חמץ into the sea, or only before scattering it to the wind?

steps.title: The same question about destroying an idol
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes a matching משנה about עבודה זרה, where רבי יוסי says to grind it, and the same question was asked there.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned something like this about עבודה זרה. רבי יוסי says: He grinds it and scatters it to the wind, or throws it into the sea. And a question was asked: What does he mean? He grinds it and scatters it to the wind, and he also grinds it and throws it into the sea? Or perhaps he grinds it and scatters it to the wind, but he may throw it into the sea whole?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the exact same question exists about destroying an idol. This sets up the next step, where רבה compares the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting חמץ and עבודה זרה side by side lets the אמוראים ask whether the two cases should have the same rule. 'Grinding' (for an idol) matches 'crumbling' (for חמץ). The question again is whether grinding is needed before throwing into the sea.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא,
phrases.english: We also learned something similar regarding idol worship:
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹחֵק וְזוֹרֶה לָרוּחַ, אוֹ מֵטִיל לַיָּם.
phrases.english: He grinds and scatters it to the wind, or throws it into the sea.
And a question was raised: what is he saying?

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹחֵק וְזוֹרֶה לָרוּחַ, וְשׁוֹחֵק וּמֵטִיל לַיָּם.
phrases.english: He grinds and scatters it to the wind, and grinds and throws it into the sea?
Or perhaps he grinds and scatters it to the wind,
but he may throw it into the sea whole.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case with the same question. רבה answers both questions in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must an idol be ground before it is thrown into the sea?

steps.title: רבה: the idol needs no grinding, but חמץ needs crumbling
steps.stepSummary: רבה reasons that an idol goes to the ים המלח, so it needs no grinding, while חמץ goes into ordinary rivers, so it needs crumbling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It makes sense that עבודה זרה, which is thrown into the ים המלח, does not need grinding. חמץ, which may be thrown into other rivers, needs crumbling.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers both questions with logic and gives the two cases different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An idol is thrown into the ים המלח, where nobody will find it or take it out, so it can go in whole. חמץ may be thrown into any river, where someone could find a whole loaf and eat it on פסח. So חמץ must be crumbled first.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it is logical

phrases.english: Rabba said: It stands to reason

phrases.aramaic: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דִּלְיָם הַמֶּלַח קָא אָזְלָא —
phrases.english: that an idol, which goes into the Dead Sea —
does not need grinding.
Leaven, which goes into other rivers —
needs crumbling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both questions using logic about where each item ends up.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Idol thrown into the sea: no grinding needed. חמץ thrown into the sea: crumbling needed.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the opposite makes more sense
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף argues the reverse: an idol does not dissolve, so it needs grinding, but חמץ dissolves in water, so it needs no crumbling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: On the contrary, the opposite makes sense. עבודה זרה does not dissolve, so it needs grinding. חמץ dissolves, so it does not need crumbling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rejects רבה's logic and flips both rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף looks at what the water does to the item, not where it is thrown. Bread falls apart in water on its own, so crumbling it adds nothing. An idol made of hard material stays whole in water, so it must be ground to be truly destroyed.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
On the contrary, the opposite stands to reason:
an idol, which does not dissolve —
needs grinding.
Leaven, which dissolves —
does not need crumbling.

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבה looked at where the item is thrown. What really matters is whether the item breaks down in water by itself.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting רבה: חמץ is crumbled even for the sea
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that each side has a supporting ברייתא, then quotes the one that matches רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that matches רבה, and a ברייתא was taught that matches רב יוסף. The one that matches רבה: If he was walking in the desert, he crumbles it and scatters it to the wind. If he was traveling on a ship, he crumbles it and throws it into the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first announces that there is a source for each opinion. This opening line sets up the next two steps. Then it quotes the ברייתא about חמץ, which supports רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא is about someone holding חמץ while traveling. Even on a ship, he must crumble the חמץ before throwing it into the sea. That fits רבה, who said חמץ needs crumbling, and goes against רב יוסף's claim that it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that supports him

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in line with Rabba,
a baraita was taught in line with Rav Yosef.
A baraita in line with Rabba:
If he was walking in the desert —
he crumbles it and scatters it to the wind.
If he was traveling on a ship —
he crumbles it and throws it into the sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that backs רבה's position on חמץ.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ruling that חמץ needs crumbling even before it is thrown into the sea.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a traveler on a ship who crumbles his חמץ before throwing it into the sea.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting רב יוסף: an idol is ground even for the sea
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about an idol requires grinding even when it is thrown into the sea, which matches רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא that matches רב יוסף: If he was walking in the desert, he grinds it and scatters it to the wind. If he was traveling on a ship, he grinds it and throws it into the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second ברייתא, about destroying an idol, which supports רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here even an idol thrown into the sea must be ground first. That fits רב יוסף, who said an idol needs grinding, and goes against רבה. The next step turns each ברייתא into a challenge against the other side.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה: an idol needs no grinding, but חמץ needs crumbling. רב יוסף: the reverse. Each one has a supporting ברייתא. Notice that the two ברייתות together actually require crushing in both cases.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ברייתות. The one that supports רבה is about חמץ (crumbling). The one that supports רב יוסף is about an idol (grinding).

phrases.english: A baraita in line with Rav Yosef:
If he was walking in the desert —
he grinds it and scatters it to the wind.
If he was traveling on a ship —
he grinds it and throws it into the sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the matching source for the other side.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's ruling that an idol needs grinding even before it is thrown into the sea.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a traveler on a ship who grinds an idol before throwing it into the sea.

steps.title: Each side faces a difficult ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא requiring grinding challenges רבה, and the ברייתא requiring crumbling challenges רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The grinding ברייתא is difficult for רבה. The crumbling ברייתא is difficult for רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that each opinion has a ברייתא that seems to go against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said an idol needs no grinding because it goes to the ים המלח, yet a ברייתא requires grinding even when it is thrown into the sea. רב יוסף said חמץ needs no crumbling because it dissolves in water, yet a ברייתא requires crumbling. So each side is now under attack.

keyTerms.meaning: Grinding into powder (said about the idol)

phrases.english: Grinding is difficult for Rabba,
phrases.notes: The idol ברייתא requires grinding, but רבה said an idol does not need it.

phrases.english: crumbling is difficult for Rav Yosef.
phrases.notes: The חמץ ברייתא requires crumbling, but רב יוסף said חמץ does not need it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחִיקָה קַשְׁיָא לְרַבָּה, פֵּירוּר קַשְׁיָא לְרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the two ברייתות just quoted into challenges against each side.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view on idols and רב יוסף's view on חמץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each ברייתא demands a step that one of the אמוראים said is unnecessary.

steps.title: רבה's answer: different bodies of water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers on רבה's behalf: grinding is needed for other rivers but not for the ים המלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Grinding is not difficult for רבה. One case is the ים המלח, and the other case is other rivers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה's view by saying the grinding ברייתא is talking about a different kind of water than his case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the idol is thrown into the ים המלח, it needs no grinding, because nobody will ever take anything out of there. The ברייתא that requires grinding is talking about other rivers, where someone could find the idol and use it. So the two sources do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: The Dead Sea, where nothing is ever recovered
This case... that case: a way of splitting two sources into two situations

phrases.english: Grinding is not difficult for Rabba:
this case is into the Dead Sea,
that case is into other rivers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources into two different cases (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to require grinding even in the place where רבה said it is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The grinding ברייתא is about other rivers. רבה's rule of no grinding applies only to the ים המלח.

steps.title: רב יוסף's answer: wheat versus bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers on רב יוסף's behalf: crumbling is needed for leavened wheat kernels but not for bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Crumbling is not difficult for רב יוסף. One case is wheat, and the other case is bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף's view by saying the crumbling ברייתא is talking about a different kind of חמץ than his case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread falls apart by itself in water, so it needs no crumbling, which is רב יוסף's rule. Leavened wheat kernels do not fall apart on their own, so they must be broken up first. That is the case of the ברייתא that requires crumbling.
steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים survive. רבה splits the idol case by the type of water (ים המלח versus other rivers). רב יוסף splits the חמץ case by the type of food (bread versus wheat).

phrases.english: Crumbling is not difficult for Rav Yosef:
this case is with wheat,
phrases.notes: Kernels do not dissolve, so they must be broken up.

phrases.english: that case is with bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the challenge in step 13 and closes the רבה and רב יוסף debate.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources into two different cases (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to require crumbling all חמץ, against רב יוסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: Crumbling is needed only for wheat kernels. Bread dissolves on its own.

steps.title: New משנה: חמץ that was owned during פסח
steps.stepSummary: A גוי's חמץ is permitted for benefit after פסח, but a Jew's חמץ is forbidden, based on the פסוק "לא יראה לך שאור".
steps.simpleTranslation: If פסח passed over חמץ that belonged to a גוי, a Jew may benefit from it. If the חמץ belonged to a Jew, benefit from it is forbidden, as the פסוק says, "no leaven shall be seen with you."
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on חמץ that stayed in someone's possession through all of פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling depends on who owned the חמץ during פסח. The פסוק says "לך", meaning "with you". That word ties the איסור to a Jew's ownership, so a גוי's חמץ is not affected.

keyTerms.meaning: חמץ that stayed in someone's possession through פסח
Permitted for benefit (for example, selling it or feeding it to animals)
"No leaven shall be seen with you" (שמות יג:ז)

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about benefit AFTER פסח is over. It is not about eating חמץ during פסח.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Leavened bread of a gentile
over which Passover has passed
is permitted for benefit,
and that of a Jew is forbidden for benefit,
as it is said: "No leaven shall be seen with you."
phrases.notes: The word "with you" ties the rule to Jewish ownership.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חָמֵץ שֶׁל גּוֹי שֶׁעָבַר עָלָיו הַפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the debate about how to destroy חמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After פסח, a גוי's חמץ is permitted for benefit, and a Jew's חמץ is forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: Who wrote this משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the author of the משנה is and says it fits none of three known תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה? It is not רבי יהודה's, not רבי שמעון's, and not רבי יוסי הגלילי's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by asking which תנא this משנה follows. It is setting up a look at the opinions of these three תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא claims that none of the three known views on חמץ after פסח matches the משנה. To show this, it must first lay out what each of them holds, so the next step begins quoting their ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the author of our משנה?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Who is the author of our mishna?
Not Rabbi Yehuda,
and not Rabbi Shimon,
and not Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the authorship of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the משנה follows, since it seems to match none of the three.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. רבי יהודה holds that חמץ before and after its time carries a לאו, and during its time a לאו and כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are these opinions? As a ברייתא teaches: with חמץ, both before its time and after its time, a person violates a לאו. During its time, he violates a לאו and gets כרת. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains its question by quoting the ברייתא that lists the three opinions, starting with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the איסור continues even after פסח, as a לאו. That means the איסור comes from the חמץ itself, so even a גוי's חמץ should be forbidden. This does not fit the משנה, which permits a גוי's חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (What are these opinions?)
Before its time: from midday of ערב פסח
After its time: after פסח is over
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating חמץ on פסח

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יהודה's view that a לאו applies even after פסח is the first opinion the גמרא will rule out as the author of the משנה.

phrases.english: What is it? As it was taught:
phrases.notes: Introduces the ברייתא with the three views.

phrases.english: Leavened bread, whether before its time
or after its time
one transgresses a negative commandment for it.
During its time,
one transgresses a negative commandment and karet,
the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to fill in the three opinions mentioned in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source of the opinions is a ברייתא. רבי יהודה's view: a לאו applies before and after פסח, and a לאו plus כרת applies during פסח.
